context: How to check whether it still happens (Windows): open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc), go to Details, and sort by CPU. On your 24-core PC, a session spinning one full core shows about 4% CPU on a claude.exe line. Several claude.exe lines sitting near 4% while you're not using them means it's still happening. Nobody knows the cause yet; it looks like a Claude Desktop issue, not claude-settings.
ref: c40 (idle desktop sessions each burn a full CPU core)
steps: Open Task Manager, Details tab, and sort by CPU.
Count the claude.exe lines near 4% each.
If there are several, archive the Claude Desktop sessions you're not using, then check again.
Optional: report it to Anthropic (Claude Desktop 3.1623.0.0, claude-code 2.1.304).
title: Archive the idle desktop sessions that spin a CPU core each
